subject: Compute commitment verification & provisional hold request - CatalystAI
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodai.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodai.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodai.com>
Cc: 
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Internal check: CatalystAI committed compute needs (POC -> GA)

Quick summary: CatalystAI (Elena) is in late-stage procurement and needs a commitment window for dedicated GPUs tied to their POC/GA timeline. They asked for a firm procurement target by EOM (Jun 30) to align enterprise purchase orders.

Key asks from customer:
- Initial POC: 12x A100-40GB equivalent (4–6 week POC starting early Aug).
- GA ramp: scale to 48 GPUs across two availability zones by Nov (steady-state).
- Ability to burst via hosted if Dedicated pool is constrained.

Attachments: Catalyst_Capacity_Specs_v3.pdf, MOP_estimate.xlsx (customer-provided sizing + our initial operational cost model).

Can infra confirm current free capacity in us-west-2 (A100 or compatible) and whether we can place a provisional hold / soft-commit for ~14 GPUs to cover the POC margin? Also call out any conflicting reservations (committed pools) that would block a hard commit.

Reason: Customer procurement requires a written indication of availability to include in their purchase approval. We want to avoid over-allocating but also not lose the deal.

Thanks — appreciate a quick scan and recommendation on: soft-hold duration, fallback plan, and whether we need Engineering to pre-qualify model quantization to fit alternate hardware.

— Ben
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Catalyst_Capacity_Specs_v3.pdf (pdf, 1.2MB)]
[Attachment: MOP_estimate.xlsx (spreadsheet, 120KB)]
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodai.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodai.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodai.com>
Cc: 
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2026 10:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Internal check: CatalystAI committed compute needs (POC -> GA)

Ben — ran a quick inventory and put together a short ops-readout. High level:

1) Usable spare (us-west-2): ~36 GPUs that match A100-40GB profiles today, but ~20 of those are in our Dedicated reserved pools slated for Q3 churn (some are under soft-hold for other opportunities).
2) Conflicts: we have a pending reserve for TR-55 (sales) that could overlap if we try to hard-commit more than 18 GPUs in Aug.
3) Suggested approach: place a 60-day soft-hold for 14 GPUs in us-west-2 (covers the POC + 2 GPU buffer). Soft-hold means we mark capacity in the allocator and block other soft-hold requests but do not physically vMotion or pin hardware.
4) Fallback config: If we need to reduce physical A100s, we can qualify Catalyst's larger-sequence models to run quantized on 80GB V100 equivalents (estimated perf delta ~8–12% latency increase). Alternatively, streamed-hosted burst is available for up to +20% token volume for short windows.

I flagged the TR-55 owner to see if we can deconflict; if they don't accept a partial release we should still be able to honor a soft-hold but not a hard-commit >18 GPUs.

Action items for us:
- Ops to place soft-hold for 14 GPUs (if Sales approves).
- Eng to run quick quantization perf check on Catalyst sample prompt set (takes ~48h).
- Sales to request procurement timeline in writing (need hard date for escalation).

If you want I can place the soft-hold now and tag it as provisional pending contract signature.

— Karthik
Sr. Infrastructure Program Manager
Redwood Inference

Ben — thanks for the quick follow-up. Confirming our ask so you have it for internal coordination:

Procurement (cc'd) will need any hold language you propose and the pricing/credit terms to draft the PO. If you can give a soft-commit now and clarify fallback (quantized on alternative hardware / hosted burst), that will be sufficient for us to proceed with internal approvals.

Appreciate the help — Elena
